title: Little expectations but a game changer
body:
Undiagnosed ADHD sufferer trying to get organised. Being able to pick routines that I want to do with my day (such as face care, kitchen clean etc) without too much brain investment is just what I need. Also it doesn’t bully you into doing your tasks which I like. I would prefer it if you could set a monthly day to do tasks as well as a date eg first Saturday of the month to do a task rather that “repeats every 21st” but that’s ok, I can reschedule it if need be. Nifty little app and unlike others meant to manage ADHD it wasn’t a horrendously expensive monthly price.
UPDATE. Rarely use it. I guess it’s a novelty factor. Also when I did try to use it and was moving tasks not completed to the next day, I noticed rows of 6 not 7 numbers, the days of the week not lining up. Come on! I have enough problem with this without your software fiddling it too

Me+ is a great app, it can help you track your sleep, your daily routine and more! I especially love the 100 ways to love yourself, it can provide me with great things to do everything. I also love the fact that there is meditation, I’m someone who struggles to stay calm so this helps! 

Things I don’t like,
Though this app may be some way to make your life healthier, it’s hard to keep up with everything. Drink 2100ML of water daily is almost impossible to me since most of the time I don’t even know how much water I’ve drank! And for the younger kids using this app 2000 water (not even minimum) is way too much water. Secondly, most of the time I’m using this app everything you need is money, as someone who wants a app with less ‘subscribing’ this app has way too much of spending money. Also the notifications. Everyday I set the notification for somethings, but the app is constantly sending me stupid notifications, this annoys me especially when I’ve had a bad day from school and came back to text or watch YouTube, every few minutes there are notifications ringing.

title: Predatory, Scarcity Marketing & Spamming
body:
I really wanted to like this app—it has numerous features that seem helpful on the surface and I like multipurpose applications—but I didn’t because the logic behind it is ugly

The initial quiz is used unethically to benefit their pockets and not the user. For example, they rely heavily on scarcity marketing tactics like countdown timers and limited time offers, with numerous stimulating flashy pop-ups and notifications. These tactics are documented to disproportionately impact neurodivergent people, so using these tactics is gross. Additionally, their notification SPAM was so great that it has sent me more notifications than any other non-messaging app.

I know this app has good marketing and is within a crowded market that’s hard to navigate, but please do not reward them with your time, attention or money.

title: Update dilemma
body:
What I like. 
- love that I can now set things in the future. Grey for setting up events and things that happen in the future like things for the kids related to school and my work as a teacher. 
- love the ability to set a time frame. It’s great to be able to set times to do things so I’m not trying to figure out what to do next.  Relieves some of the cognitive load and executive dysfunction related to ADHD. 
-the new images/icons are great but not necessarily a needed update. 

What I miss. 

-timers and number of times features related to tasks. A 20-tidy task now involves the extra step of opening a new app for a timer. Without it, there is another layer to completing a task I don't need. 
- the description under the task name. I used this to write why the task is important or a motivational quote to know my why. To open the app after my auto update to see this as part of my subset was a challenge and time-consuming to either remove or mark off to complete the task. 

I found the app trying to find something to improve my habits that worked with my ADHD because the stress is not helping me get my ADHD under control. These small things leaving could mean having to find a new app or continually fighting myself to stay motivated.

title: Promotes shame and disordered eating behaviours
body:
The whole app focuses on shaming your current self, which isn’t a very sustainable way to change your habits to healthy, lasting ones. 

There is too much of a focus on weight loss, rather than on healthy behaviours (which may mean you happen to lose weight). It also gives some disordered eating advice like “being a little hungry is the best thing that can happen to you.” This isn’t true - if you want to eat sustainably and healthily, you should nourish yourself and feel satisfied. It also suggests only having black coffee or tea because these are appetite suppressants. Again, having black coffee/tea isn’t a satisfying, and diverse meal. It’s way healthier to have food that actually satisfies you and is nutritious. Also it’s ok to have some milk with your tea, it tastes nicer (plus adds protein)

Also shaming yourself around eating junk food can lend towards a cycle of restriction and binging. Instead, giving yourself permission to eat junk food, while also being guided by gentle nutrition and how your body feels is much healither way. Look up into intuitive eating for more advice

title: Great concept, could use improvement in areas.
body:
The app is great but I found it quite overwhelming at first. The discover area where you could just add specific things, I thought was great but then it became too much trying to adjust and customise everything that I had to just delete it all (which also was confusing). 

I think an area where you can see ALL of your habits, ALL of your DELETED habits, and REMOVED habits would be great! As a good reference point, as well as a good place to delete any habits you aren’t happy with.

The “goal” feature is a bit difficult because (for example) it doesn’t have the option of “L” or “drinks” for a habit like “Drink Water”. Or perhaps for habits you only want to accomplish at least 3x a month? 

It would be great if it included a “Goal” in terms of how many times you would like to achieve this habit in a month. But maybe that’s just me? 

I ended up deleting everything and starting from scratch, creating my own tags and colours and habits. The app glitched ALOT during this and I kept having to close and re-open, but I got there in the end :) It’s great being able to tick things off. Although, I don’t understand why my day on the calendar becomes a silver medal? And I also got what looked like a baby chick and “3x” or something pop up? As a reward??? Idk. More explanation would be great.

The recordings are quite accurate distinguishing between snoring, talking, environment etc. The only thing that would make it that much better is if the daily horoscope and fact could be read in full. At the moment I can only read the thumbnail preview on the daily screen.
author: Diandra_Reviews

title: Love this app!!, but can’t subscribe :-(
body:
I downloaded this app to check it out and I absolutely love it!! Great alarm concepts, sleep recording (snoring, talking other random sounds etc) and actually categorised for you the next morning for review. Also gives a nightly sleep score. Also has lots of good meditation/relaxation clips to listen to. 

ONE PROBLEM: I can’t seem to subscribe!!! :-(. When I click on the 50% discount special to scribe it says “Subscription Failed -Please try again”. Very frustrating. Can someone fix this asap? Take my money!!!!!! :-)
author: Oz_guy
